title: Superlinear randomized Turing-machine time lower bounds in linear-time Sigma3
author: Emanuele Viola
work: Pseudorandom Bits and Lower Bounds for Randomized Turing Machines
source_version: Theory of Computing18 (2022), Article10, publisher source publicationMay 20, 2022; DOI10.4086/toc.2022.v018a010

source_locator.proof_scope: Complete author argument including supplied core constructions

difficulty_reason: The superlinear lower bound combines the new random-tape generator with a resource-sensitive nondeterministic simulation of a machine on generated bits. Section4 builds that simulator with sublinear space and guessing cost before closing an alternation/time-hierarchy contradiction, a substantive lower-bound obligation beyond routine qualification-level hierarchy arguments.

source_check.note: Full source retains the generator and its crossing-sequence core plus the new nondeterministic, small-space simulation with direct generated-bit queries. Alternation/time tradeoffs, the time-efficient probabilistic simulation and hierarchy theorem remain precisely referenced prerequisites. Theorem1.2 constructs a pseudorandom generator for two-tape RTMs, while Theorem1.4 gives a time lower bound for three-tape RTM2 computations. The latter has a separate new Section4 simulation and hierarchy contradiction, so it is not merely a complementary or parameter-restated formulation of the generator. Supporting simulation Theorem2.2 and both claims stay uncounted.
